Nikon Preset 0.5.6-beta - Delivery and validation record

The size and SHA-256 above were read from the frozen artifact and checked again
for the final log audit. The Android UI observations below used this final APK.
Completed synthetic checks and outstanding physical-device work are separated.

PHONE AND CAMERA STATUS AT RECORD CREATION

The user's PKG110 / Android 16 phone previously received 0.5.5-beta (code 22).
It was not online through ADB during this investigation. No valid new phone
last-report, pending journal or system/network-state capture was obtained,
and 0.5.6 has not yet been installed on that phone. Do not infer a current
permission or battery-exemption state from older inspection records.

No physical camera, camera hotspot or physical-phone interface was operated
for this validation. Phone permissions were not changed. Existing Z6II user
feedback remains distinct from developer-observed interoperability evidence.

CHANGES IN THIS BUILD

- Explicitly confirmed replacement of occupied C1-C9 slots is supported over
  Wi-Fi and USB. The confirmation UI lists all nine slots, prefers an empty
  target, and shows the original name for an occupied target. Replacement
  requires a separate final confirmation naming both old and new presets.
- Existing backend APIs remain empty-only by default. Replacement overloads
  require an immutable OverwriteConfirmation containing a private copy of the
  originally confirmed occupied slot. Target, exact bytes, SHA-256, name and
  base must match both the fresh nine-slot scan and the adjacent pre-write
  target read. Changed or newly empty targets stop without a registration.
- Fresh NCP conversion, device/capability checks, a single SetPicCtrlData
  attempt and exact same-target readback remain required. There is no generic
  write-budget reset, automatic retry, rollback or atomic compare-and-set.
  Wi-Fi success retains the verified session and both sockets for another
  separately confirmed operation. USB still requires acknowledged cleanup.
- USB replacement uses WRITE_CONFIRMED_PC. Its only additional read allowance
  compared with the old empty-slot mode is 0x90CF with Standard=1. Payload,
  target, new=0 and one-write transport restrictions remain intact.
- Reports preserve overwrite intent, the confirmed original hash/name/base
  and target, fresh capability verification and both snapshot-match results.
  Occupied-target success does not falsely mark the target as initially empty.
- The durable pending journal records overwrite intent and the original
  hash/name before backend entry. A P2 recovery-state issue was fixed by
  carrying immutable journal JSON with application-owned ImportStatus, so
  Activity recreation restores the same pending intent. Unknown results are
  read and compared; they do not automatically replay a replacement.
- Read-only Picture Control heartbeat can retain a still-healthy owned session
  after a complete, matching GeneralError (0x2002) or DeviceBusy (0x2019).
  Backend and runtime share the response classification. The refusal remains
  an exception with diagnostics, not a successful data read. Other codes,
  wrong transactions, invalid datasets, cancellation and protocol/network
  failures remain terminal. A write-phase 0x2002 is never exempt or replayed.
- Album grids and immersive viewing prefer an advertised Nikon GetLargeThumb
  (0x90C4) camera-generated JPEG preview, with bounded transfer and the existing
  GetThumb fallback. Viewing does not invoke GetObject. The original is fetched
  only after an explicit download action. Large-preview metadata is retained
  in the preview cache, and album mode does not gain registration permission.
- On-device synthetic UI work exposed grid bitmap-cache thrashing. The final
  fix captures actual grid geometry on the main thread, caps grid decoding
  at 320 pixels and budgets the visible set against 10 MiB. Strict sampling
  keeps decoded grid images within that target. Remote and local grids use
  the same policy; detail-view decoding remains separate and unchanged.

Independent source review reported no remaining P1/P2 findings within the
reviewed import, ownership, recovery and preview scope after the recovery-state
fix. This is a scoped review result, not a real-camera or comprehensive UX
certification.

USER-REPORTED DISCONNECT AND EVIDENCE LIMIT

The user reported that, on installed 0.5.5, the phone's system Wi-Fi connection
to the camera also disconnected after preset import, and subsequently clarified
that the camera body itself turns off its hotspot. The phone was offline when
a new report was requested, so the actual failure response, network sequence
and camera-side trigger remain unknown. This is user feedback, not an observed
physical-camera trace from the synthetic validation below.

Source review independently confirmed a premature-close path: a matched,
complete Standard heartbeat GeneralError still released an otherwise healthy
session. This build removes that specific close path under the existing
identity, transaction, ownership and protocol checks. That code correction
does not prove the user's incident was caused by GeneralError, that the camera
disabled its access point for this reason, or that physical-camera stability
has been established. No automatic reconnect or write replay was added.

REGRESSION RESULTS

20982 checks passed in total:
- 9505 core checks, including PTP/IP 3956, album host 226 and preview cache 53.
- 11477 Picture Control probe checks: ordinary USB 685, read-only Picture
  Control 453, USB copy/adaptation 1253 and wireless 9086.

The replacement regressions cover unchanged empty-only defaults, immutable
original-target evidence, fresh capability checks, changes at both target
reads, cancellation after matching recheck but before Set, exact replacement
readback, unknown outcomes and a second explicitly confirmed replacement on
the same connection. Heartbeat cases cover matching GeneralError followed by
a successful tick, wrong-transaction/nonrecoverable errors, post-import
temporary refusal, subsequent explicit import and terminal write GeneralError.
Synthetic peer self-tests preserve the original empty-slot scenario alongside
the occupied-slot and post-import temporary-refusal scenarios.

These host/regression counts do not establish Android service scheduling,
physical installation, camera hotspot behavior or native photographic effects.

COMPLETED FINAL-APK ALBUM UI / PROTOCOL OBSERVATIONS

Environment: Pixel 9 emulator, Android 17, 1080 x 2424 portrait display.
Peer: loopback-only synthetic camera and JPEG fixtures; no camera hardware.
Artifact: exactly the frozen APK hash recorded above.

Archived evidence:
- docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-functional.log
- docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-before-download.log
- docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-after-download.log
- docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-large.log

The static portrait grid completed 15 large-preview requests and remained
stable without repeated grid requests. Before explicit download there were
zero GetObject requests. Immersive detail displayed a 1280 x 800 high-quality
preview; that intentional detail read brought total large previews to 16.

Only the explicit original-download action produced GetObject (0x1009) for
TEST3 / handle 3: exactly one original transfer of 89320 bytes. The archived
before/after logs distinguish preview traffic from that original transfer.

The downloaded emulator file was independently pulled without run-as and its
89320-byte size and SHA-256 matched the local fixture TEST_0003.JPG:

Independent audit copy: app/build/v056-download-audit-TEST_0003.JPG
The full emulator/fixture hash evidence is archived in the functional log.

The landscape observation did not add repeated preview or original requests.
The existing download-status message left little vertical space for the grid
in that configuration; this baseline layout limitation remains. These checks
verify the stated functionality and request counts, not comprehensive landscape
or visual-quality certification.

COMPLETED FINAL-APK FALLBACK PREVIEW CHECK

Archive: docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-fallback.log.
The synthetic peer advertised GetLargeThumb but explicitly rejected its first
request with OperationNotSupported (0x2005). Independent log counting found
exactly one 0x90C4 request, then 16 GetThumb (0x100A) requests and zero GetObject
requests. The unsupported large-preview operation was not repeatedly probed
within that session. The operator observed the 320 x 200 fallback detail and
its preview-source indication. This establishes the tested fallback behavior,
not support for every camera error or image format.

COMPLETED FINAL-APK REPLACEMENT / RETAINED-CONNECTION AUDIT

Archives:
- docs/device-review/wireless-0.5.6-overwrite.log
- docs/device-review/album-0.5.6-functional.log

The loopback-only peer seeded occupied C1 with SYNTHETIC OLD. At
03:34:41.871Z the operator canceled its replacement confirmation dialog;
there were zero virtual writes at that checkpoint. The first registration
did not occur until a later explicit confirmation. No real slot was accessed.

The occupied C1 replacement was explicitly confirmed in a 375dp-wide
configuration (1080 physical pixels, density 460 dpi), dark theme, font scale
1.3 and system animations disabled. Its fresh capability request was tx60,
the full nine-slot scan tx61-69, adjacent C1 recheck tx70, registration tx71
and exact readback tx72. The original C1 SHA-256 was
b47c803b00e75cfd0e71377f9eaab7da5e39a74c5c58aad88a4a46c14bef5781.

The first post-import Standard heartbeat, tx73 at 03:36:59.786Z, received the
intentional complete matched 0x2002 refusal. No close/reconnect followed.
The next periodic Standard request was tx74 at 03:37:09.796Z on the same
session. A second separately confirmed import into empty C2 then completed
on the same sockets: fresh capability tx91, all nine slots tx92-100, adjacent
C2 recheck tx101, registration tx102 and exact readback tx103.

Both 614-byte virtual registrations and their immediate readbacks had SHA-256:
07434caabeee4bc79727b3cbfd105e037659933866e5aada76419db8745bb199
The log records exactly two writes, only one replacing the seeded occupied
target. Repeated later C1 reads during a refresh are not additional writes.

Independently recomputed connection/transaction totals:
- One InitCommand, one InitEvent, one OpenSession and one CloseSession.
- One session throughout; 120 commands total: two at tx0, then positive
  transaction IDs exactly 1 through 118, with no gaps or repeats.
- OpenSession 03:33:01.499Z to CloseSession 03:40:06.658Z: 425.159 seconds.
- Standard requests total 46. Four were initial/refresh reads (tx2, 17, 44,
  79), leaving 42 periodic heartbeat attempts, including the one simulated
  0x2002 refusal. The peer's summary heartbeats=45 includes three refresh
  reads and must not be reported as 45 periodic timer heartbeats.
- CloseSession was tx118, after the final explicit manual disconnect; no
  intervening session close, reinitialization or additional registration.

Density/theme restoration rebuilt the Activity while retaining the successful
C2 outcome and connection. The functional trace records Home plus screen off
at 03:38:50.8644254Z and the asleep checkpoint at 03:39:48.1579093Z, an interval
of 57.293 seconds. Five periodic Standard requests occurred within that
interval. The checkpoint showed the connectedDevice service in the foreground,
the application's partial CPU wake lock held and the screen asleep. Settings
still showed the connection after returning. This was ordinary background /
screen-off verification; no new forced-Doze claim is made for this version.

The operator initiated manual disconnect at 03:40:04.432Z. Only then did the
peer receive CloseSession at 03:40:06.658Z. The functional trace subsequently
showed no running connection service and zero wake locks, with the application
CPU-lock release recorded at 03:40:06.720. No automatic reconnect occurred.

The operator visually inspected the large-preview detail, the light-theme
occupied-slot confirmation dialog and the dark 375dp/font-1.3 confirmation
dialog, finding those captures readable without clipping. Other states were
checked through the recorded hierarchy/screenshots and protocol traces. This
limited pixel inspection is not a general accessibility, every-size or UX
certification; the landscape baseline limitation noted above remains.

OUTSTANDING PHYSICAL-DEVICE VALIDATION

- The phone remains offline through ADB. This 0.5.6 artifact has not been
  installed on it; a later installation needs its own version/hash check.
- No physical camera body or hotspot was operated. Obtain the user's actual
  report/network evidence and test physical-camera interoperability before
  claiming the camera-side hotspot issue is resolved.
- Synthetic responses and successful connection retention cannot establish
  Nikon firmware policy, vendor power-management behavior or native image
  appearance. No phone permissions were changed.

Historical 0.5.5 lifecycle/Doze and phone-install evidence retains its original
version scope and must not be relabeled as 0.5.6 evidence.
